top_story.headline: A quiet day: no new disclosures or FARA filings, and two lobbying reports that name top officials
top_story.dek: Nothing in today's input rises to a lead; the Senate disclosure feed failed to load.
paragraphs: No House or Senate financial disclosures, FARA filings or OGE items of note came in for this window, and the Senate eFD fetch returned an error, so Senate filings could not be checked.

The closest items are two third-quarter lobbying reports in the LDA data: one from the Leadership Conference on Civil and Human Rights that names Todd Blanche, and an amendment from the Motor & Equipment Manufacturers Association listing the Vice President among the entities lobbied. Both are detailed in the Contacts section.

sections.eyebrow: Contacts With the President, VP & Cabinet
sections.headline: Two lobbying reports name top officials; no FARA contacts
paragraphs: No FARA filings in the window were flagged for the President, Vice President or cabinet. Two LDA filings name a top official or the Vice President. The input does not show the full context of either reference.

items: Leadership Conference on Civil and Human Rights (self-filed, third-quarter report): the filing names Todd Blanche. Lobbying topics include the blocking of senior officer promotions, Consumer Financial Protection Bureau policy and oversight, cryptocurrency regulation and bills such as H.R. 7866 and H.R. 10184. LDA filing.

Motor & Equipment Manufacturers Association (self-filed, third-quarter amendment): the entities lobbied include the Vice President. Topics include preventing imports of counterfeit automotive parts, vehicle technology and consumer access to vehicle data. LDA filing.

sections.headline: No notable ethics filings this period
paragraphs: Routine financial disclosures and ethics filings from executive branch officials are processed daily by the Office of Government Ethics. This period had 42 filings total, all routine.

sections.headline: No new House or Senate filings in the input
paragraphs: The input held no House or Senate disclosures that earlier editions had not already reported. The Senate eFD fetch failed with a parsing error, so the Senate count reflects a failed check, not a confirmed absence of filings.

sections.headline: 12 new registrations and 6 terminations, led by defense-tech and cybersecurity clients
paragraphs: The LDA feed held 283 filings posted since October 26: 202 third-quarter reports, 27 third-quarter no-activity reports, 14 third-quarter amendments, 12 registrations, 4 registration amendments and 6 terminations (including no-activity and amendment variants), plus assorted late-quarter amendments and reports. Below are all registrations and terminations and five notable activity reports; the other 260 filings are left out as routine or signal-free.

Revere Federal Strategies filed a large share of the activity reports, with dozens of small defense-tech clients each paying about $10,000 to $45,000 for the quarter and a former House Armed Services Committee staffer listed as the covered position.
